matches.quote: Some other mechanism is needed, such as strain, bubbles or interlayer-spacing variation. These are again fabrication effects rather than twist
Only one twisted device is reported; device-to-device reproducibility is not addressed.
The gradual energy changes at spots 2 and 3 are attributed to a canted state... The data can also be read as partial domain switching.
In Fig. 2d, the twisted c-axis data reach only about 1.323 eV at ±2 T... h_⊥y ≈ 1.9 T is read essentially at the edge of the sweep range
The hard-axis anisotropy h_y rises from 1.06 T (pristine) to 1.42–1.61 T (twisted)... the authors' own premise is that twisting "primarily tunes" interlayer exchange.
Spot-to-spot variation is unexplained. Small twist-angle inhomogeneity would not produce the different h_E values found at the three spots... Some other mechanism is needed, such as strain
Real first-order switching proceeds by nucleation and domain-wall propagation at defects and edges... A spot-averaged mixture of AP and P domains would also give an intermediate apparent peak energy.
Several factors other than twist can reduce interlayer exchange and change switching behaviour: ... heterostrain introduced during pickup at 100 °C; a different dielectric and strain environment
The confocal spot (~1 µm) averages over very many moiré cells... the regime of validity ("small moiré wavelength", "strong intralayer exchange") is never quantified.
If switching is nucleation-limited, the hysteresis width in the twisted sample may be governed by pinning and nucleation barriers rather than by h_E.
state whether Ref. 33 predicts sign changes of the local interlayer exchange... the averaged exchange is reduced by registry-dependent cancellation while the hopping magnitude is not
compare these to the relevant magnetic length, e.g. √(A/J_inter) with A the intralayer stiffness... state whether Ref. 33 predicts sign changes of the local interlayer exchange
However, the quantity the model gets wrong is h_AP+, the AP→P switching field, and this is precisely the field that sets the hysteresis width.

notes: C1 is marked 'partly' because the SI model actually varies h_x and h_y, which R1 missed when criticizing the main text's exchange-only attribution, while the review (P11) spotted the 50% jump in extracted h_y in Table S2 and criticized the same inconsistency with the exchange-only premise. C10 and C3 are marked 'partly' because the review identifies the exact same underlying issues (partial domain switching at spots 2/3 and fabrication-induced strain) but requests spectral lineshape fitting and a 0-degree stack control rather than minor loops at spot 3 or a strain map.
